✦ Pocket oracle · design goal

A helper that keeps talking after the router dies

Lights drop, search pages follow, chat windows follow too. Our oracle aims to dwell inside your handset instead: type any worry, receive a brief, sourced reply instantly.

  • ✓
    Lives in local storage

    Fetch it one time over broadband at home. Afterwards each reply is produced internally; nothing you type travels anywhere.

  • ✓
    Shows its homework

    Replies are lifted from reviewed safety sheets and name the sheet used. When nothing fits, it admits that rather than bluffing.

  • ✓
    Danger jumps the queue

    Hints of injury or leaking gas trigger exactly one instruction first: ring the rescue line.

  • ✓
    Speaks your tongue

    Instructions should arrive in multiple languages, each figure preserved exactly.

Freezer went quiet ages ago. Safe to eat that ice cream?
Likely no. Packed freezers stay frosty roughly one day if sealed. Items softened then refrozen go straight to rubbish.
Source: frozen food sheet
Heat my flat by leaving the oven ajar?
Never. Cookers produce fumes, not safe warmth. Wear layers, seal one room, huddle together.
Source: indoor warmth sheet

Sample exchanges that show the intended tone. A compact assistant can slip, so it will always point at its source sheet.

Field notes

Small habits that carry a dark evening

Food

No peeking

Each opening wastes chill you cannot recover. Choose your items first, then reach.

Warmth

Shrink the house

Pick one room, hang a blanket over the doorway, gather everyone and every cushion inside it.

Air

Engines live outside

Generators and camp stoves belong far from windows. Exhaust is odourless and merciless.

Water

Fill before it fades

Upon first flicker, fill bottles plus the tub. Taps may run dry once pumps lose electricity.

Power

Ration the battery

Lower brightness, silence alerts, close apps. One healthy battery beats five dying ones.

Signal

Agree a meeting spot

Choose some corner reachable walking, so a mute handset never equals a missing person.

Roadmap

Four stages, one direction

Cheapest useful piece first, extra reach afterwards. Stage one gets our attention; later stages follow once earlier ones hold.

  1. Stage 1 · Building
    Pocket web kit

    Oracle, atlas, triage ladder, beam, airwaves, all executing inside any handset or laptop browser.

  2. Stage 2 · Queued
    Native handset app

    Installable software passing text and speech between neighbouring handsets via nearby radio links, display dark included.

  3. Stage 3 · Queued
    Wide-area units

    Compact transmitters linking to our software, stretching a text over entire metropolitan areas.

  4. Stage 4 · Queued
    Relief wallet

    Open treasury buying radios plus kits for struggling regions; every payment traceable by anyone.

FAQ

Straight answers

Is anything usable today?

Partly at best. Stage one remains under construction, and this page tracks progress candidly. Roadmap labels separate building from merely queued.

Why attach a coin?

Hosting, cartography and transmitters cost cash. A coin supplies community plus treasury, free of advertising or subscriptions.

Which address is real?

Unannounced. The top slot stays blank and every trade link stays lifeless until we publish one. Anybody offering a different string is guessing.

What do those rows display?

Live rows for ten heavily promoted Solana tokens pulled off a free screener. Context only, never endorsement, unaffected by whatever we hold.

Could assistants function offline?

Design target, yes: a compact model plus vetted reference sheets stored locally, so nothing leaves your handset. Quality gets tested openly before any claim.

How do texts hop between handsets?

Every handset running our software passes texts to whichever neighbour sits within radio reach, repeating until the destination appears, otherwise waiting for better paths.

Is this financial advice?

Negative. Darkout ranks as memecoin. Prices swing violently, possibly reaching zero. Risk only sums you could lose without worry.
